current_leader.name: Merchant settlement acceleration decision engine
current_leader.state_transition: processor balance becomes available -> standard settlement is free/slower while accelerated settlement has a fee -> external bank/AP obligations reveal how much cash is actually needed before standard settlement -> accelerate only the minimum justified amount -> avoid unnecessary settlement fees without causing a cash shortfall
current_leader.why_survived: Current processors expose a recurring speed-versus-fee decision with machine-readable balances and payout state. Stripe publishes 1%-1.5% Instant Payout fees by region and exposes instant_available balances plus payout APIs; Indian processors publish several acceleration tiers from same-day to instant. Treasury suites forecast cash gaps, but this run did not find a sufficiently close cross-processor product whose narrow job is to combine processor balance, free settlement ETA, external bank balance and near-term obligations to compute the minimum amount worth accelerating.
current_leader.closest_threat: Broad treasury systems such as Open Money and FlowOne already forecast liquidity and optimize payment timing. First-party processors could absorb the feature if they gain external bank/AP context.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read processor available/instant-available balance and standard settlement ETA; read authorized bank balance plus obligations due before that ETA; compute and recommend the minimum accelerated amount whose fee is economically justified. Do not initiate money movement in v1.
current_leader.monetization: Small fee per successful decision or capped share of verified accelerated-settlement fees avoided relative to a documented liquidity baseline.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The avoidable fee pool may be too small if merchants rarely use paid acceleration or use it only when genuinely necessary. Gate 8 also remains open because treasury suites may already be close enough to absorb the decision.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify unnecessary use of paid accelerated settlements and attack exact competition across Stripe/Cashfree/Razorpay/PayU plus treasury suites. Kill if avoidable acceleration fees are immaterial or if an incumbent already computes the minimum amount to accelerate from processor balances plus external obligations.

recent_cross_family_findings: Paid merchant settlement acceleration creates a recurring option-value decision: Stripe charges 1%-1.5% Instant Payout fees depending on region, while Indian processors publish lower-cost same-day/next-day alternatives and on-demand settlement choices.
The potentially open micro-wedge is not faster payouts; it is calculating the minimum amount that should be accelerated using processor balances plus external cash obligations.
Cloud-storage early-deletion timing was rejected because delaying deletion usually does not reduce minimum-duration cost; providers charge the remaining minimum period either as storage or penalty.

Small-object cold-tier optimization is substantially covered by AWS/FinOps tooling and first-party smart/intelligent tiering; Azure also paused its planned 128 KiB cooler-tier billing floor in June 2026.
Chargeback contest-versus-accept scoring is already occupied by products exposing win probabilities and automated evidence/representment.
known_rejected_or_demoted_summary: Full historical rejection list is preserved in prior anchor blobs and immutable run files. Do not revive prior rejected families without materially new mechanism/evidence.
